name: I'll Do It
tagline: You say yes before you know how.
epigraph: The rye this drink calls for was first made in a barn, by amateurs.
language_row: Wren's 4-gram runs (the lint's own `ngrams()`) against every pour: clean after her cuts (16 collisions in v1, and "a book I trust", which echoed *Whoever Comes In*). "First" only as a sequence ("their first bottles", "first made"); never "hero" as praise, "a way in", "make it look easy", "anyone can", the UK press sense of a have-a-go hero, Jamie Oliver or the lobbying. "he" only for Erenzo and Lee (lint warnings accepted by Wren). The name's *Top Gear* echo is owned in Names. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/ralph-erenzo-tuthilltown.md` (F1–F25, C1–C4): *Oxford Companion* HUDSON (pdf 1037, Max Watman) and CRAFT DISTILLING (pdf 592–593); AP, "Artisan distilleries finding a high-end niche", 15 July 2007 (via NBC News); Matt Logan, interview with Ralph Erenzo, Gunks Climbers' Coalition, c. 2015; Richard Thomas, *The Whiskey Reviewer*, April 2017; *Hudson Valley One*, 11 May 2021; *HV Magazine*, 2016; New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets, 2015; State Liquor Authority counts, 2017; *Stateline*; *The Spirits Business*, 15 Sep 2020 (the rename to Do The Rye Thing); the maker's site (46%); Wikipedia, *Top Gear* (the name's echo only). Craft: *Cocktail Codex* p. 22 (split base, rye and apple brandy "magical"). Audits: `work/regular-guy-hero/historian-audit-v1.md`, `-v2.md`, `-v3.md`. Room notes: `work/regular-guy-hero/`.
names_note: **I'll Do It**, the room's pick (all three, r5): the half of the sentence this person always says, out loud, before they know how; the reading's "the second half you swallow" stays unspent. *How Hard Can It Be* was Tomás's pick through r4 and Wren's in r3; Hester sourced that *Top Gear*'s challenges ran "with the tagline 'How hard can it be?'", which puts a celebrity's voice in the title where the guest's own should be, and Tomás conceded in r5. Also considered: *Need a Hand* (Wren's second; gives the closing line's position away), *From the Ground Up* (said of Gable, F13).
open_items: **Not a mill:** the still stood on the upper floor of a barn; the gristmill had been "since sold" by 2007 (AP, F25). Any mill in the reading or the image was struck; "mill" survives only in y1's true 2001 purchase.

**Today's bottle:** Hudson Manhattan Rye is now sold as Do The Rye Thing (95% rye, 5% malted barley, 46%), owned by William Grant. Never "their rye" in the present tense, never "100% New York rye" for today's bottle.

**Point 5 without the lobbying:** the result for others is the state's 2015 line only ("one of more than 100 craft distilleries", "a model"); never 16 → 117, never that Tuthilltown caused the growth, never the 2007 Farm Distillery Act (Erenzo lobbied for it: the Campaigner's ground).

**Dossier only:** "don't quit your day job" and "learn from an expert" (F19, the guest's own fear in his voice); "had to invent" the safety rules (F20, the Innovator's word); the years and fees (sources disagree, C1–C2); Baby Bourbon before the rye (C3); the 2010 sale; Gable's death.

**Single-source quotes:** "I'm building a distillery – I need your help!" is Ralph recalling it in his son's 2021 obituary (*Hudson Valley One*); "complete amateurs" is that paper's judgement. The tea kettle is a reporter's paraphrase and is not used.
**History share:** 56% raw, 45% without the signposted reveal (Wren). Noted for Robin.
**The apple brandy is not their vodka:** it stands for their first go (a vodka from New York apples, F3, F21), and the reading says so plainly.
